name: Incomplete Congenital Stationary Night Blindness, Schubert-Bornschein Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Electroretinographic and clinical criteria for CSNB

criteria.description: Congenital night blindness (nyctalopia) present from early childhood
Characteristic electronegative electroretinogram (ERG) with normal a-wave and reduced b-wave amplitudes
Non-progressive mild to moderate reduction in visual acuity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital night blindness plus characteristic electronegative ERG
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by electrophysiological testing; genetic testing may confirm subtype.

pathognomonic.notes: Present from infancy or early childhood
Characteristic ERG finding distinguishing Schubert-Bornschein type
searchTerms: abnormal negative pattern on eye test

common.notes: Involuntary eye movements may be present
Light sensitivity reported in some patients

occasional.notes: Visual disturbances such as flashes of light

occasional.symptomName: Mild nystagmus exacerbated by low light
occasional.notes: Nystagmus may worsen in dim conditions
searchTerms: mild involuntary eye movements worse in dim light

rare.symptomName: Electronegative ERG with additional cone dysfunction
rare.notes: Rare variant with combined rod-cone involvement
searchTerms: abnormal ERG with cone cell problems
electronegative ERG with color vision loss

rare.notes: Occasional mild retinal changes on imaging

imaging: Normal fundus examination or mild retinal pigment epithelium changes
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) typically normal or subtle outer retinal layer abnormalities
other: Electroretinogram showing characteristic electronegative waveform with preserved a-wave and reduced b-wave

distinguishingFeatures: Complete CSNB shows absent rod responses on ERG
Different ERG pattern with absent b-wave
Progressive vision loss with peripheral field constriction

redFlags: Severe photophobia or pain indicating alternative diagnosis
references: Schubert G, Bornschein H. Congenital stationary night blindness with negative electroretinogram. Am J Ophthalmol. 1952.
